summary: Background: Serum urate testing requires venipuncture; urine dipstick testing is inexpensive and routine. Whether dipstick results add information on hyperuricemia beyond age, sex, and BMI is unknown. Objective: This study aims to develop and externally validate machine learning models estimating the probability of hyperuricemia from 9 dipstick fields, age, sex, and BMI, and to quantify what the dipstick adds. Methods: The development dataset included 129,535 adults with first urine tests and same-day serum urate and BMI measurements at a Korean tertiary hospital (2010-2025); 21,124 had urate levels ≥7.0 mg/dL, and 81.6% (n=105,704) had a same-day health checkup. Calibrated 12-input ensembles of Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) were trained on a person-level 80% split (103,628 persons) for serum urate ≥7.0 mg/dL (primary) and ≥9.0 mg/dL (secondary). They were tested in the remaining 25,907 persons (4225 events at ≥7.0 mg/dL) and in 49,987 adults in the KNHANES (Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey; 2016-2024; 5068 events). Inputs, KNHANES coding, split, and training procedure were fixed before fitting. We assessed discrimination, calibration, operating points by sex, decision curves, and increments over age-sex-BMI models. Results: At ≥7.0 mg/dL, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.825 (95% CI 0.820-0.831) internally and 0.845 (95% CI 0.840-0.849) externally, but 0.710 in men and 0.795 in women. Across 4 model classes, the dipstick added 0.017 to 0.024 to the external AUROC of age-sex-BMI models (0.814-0.823), or 3.1 cases per 1000 screened with top-10% referral. Externally, the models overpredicted (observed-to-expected ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.75); an intercept update fitted in half of KNHANES restored it to 1.00 in the other half. The internally derived 80%-sensitivity threshold flagged 29.8% (14,916/49,987) of adults, 97.4% (14,533/14,916) of them men; sensitivity was 77.1% (3907/5068) overall but 10.1% (53/527) in women, and positive predictive value (PPV) was 26.2% (3907/14,916). Flagging all men gave 89.6% (4541/5068) sensitivity and slightly less net benefit than the model at threshold probabilities up to 10%. At ≥9.0 mg/dL, external results were AUROC 0.860, increment 0.052 to 0.074 (1.6 cases per 1000), observed-to-expected ratio 0.48, scaled Brier score 0.002 (no better than predicting the prevalence), and PPV 2.6% at 82% sensitivity. Conclusions: Routine dipstick results add a small increment to age, sex, and BMI for identifying serum urate ≥7.0 mg/dL. Ranking transferred from the hospital to a national survey sample, but absolute risk did not, and at the tested thresholds the models mainly selected men. Both cohorts comprised people who had blood drawn, so triage of serum urate testing in urine-only encounters, in which BMI is usually missing, remains an untested hypothesis. Before any use, the models would need local recalibration and evaluation in the intended setting.
title: Machine Learning Models Combining Routine Urine Dipstick Results With Age, Sex, and BMI to Triage Serum Urate Testing: Development and External Validation Study

summary: Background: Head circumference (HC) is a routine clinical parameter in pediatric patients indicating brain growth and neurodevelopment. Although usually obtained with a tape measure, this method is operator-dependent and prone to variability. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides a retrospective alternative, but existing imaging-based approaches can be limited by predefined measurement planes, restricted clinician review, and cranial surface artifacts. Objective: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a clinician-guided software tool for measuring pediatric HC from routinely acquired 3D MRI examinations. Methods: We developed a desktop application in Python using PySide6, the Insight Segmentation and Registration Toolkit, and the Visualization Toolkit for MRI-based HC measurement. The workflow included outer skin surface reconstruction, placement of 3 landmarks to define a freely orientable measurement plane, contour extraction, and circumference calculation. Optional Delaunay-based interpolation was implemented to reduce the influence of local cranial surface irregularities. In this retrospective evaluation, the tool was applied to 23 pediatric MRI examinations, including 18 without and 5 with clinically identified cranial surface irregularities. Two clinicians independently performed 3 repeated software measurements per examination. Median software measurements were compared with a single tape-based HC measurement obtained on the date of MRI. Agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, mean absolute error (MAE), proportional bias analysis, and a linear mixed-effects model. Interrater differences and preliminary usability feedback were also evaluated. Results: Software-based HC measurement was feasible in all 23 examinations. In cases without cranial surface irregularities, the raw and interpolated contours showed similar agreement with tape-based measurements (bias 0.415 cm and 0.410 cm; MAE 0.429 cm and 0.423 cm, respectively). In the 5 examinations with irregularities, the intersection contour showed a greater bias of 1.420 cm and wider limits of agreement (LoA; −0.182 to 3.021 cm), whereas the interpolated contour showed a lower bias of 0.448 cm and narrower LoA (−0.119 to 1.014 cm). The estimated coefficient for the contour-by-subgroup interaction was −0.967 cm (SE 0.195 cm, 95% CI −1.349 to −0.584 cm; <.001). No statistically significant proportional trend was detected, although the analysis had limited power to exclude proportional bias. Interrater differences were small. The 2 clinicians reported System Usability Scale scores of 92.5 and 95.0, representing preliminary descriptive feedback. Conclusions: The clinician-guided workflow enabled MRI-based HC measurement in all examined cases and showed small interrater differences. Delaunay-based interpolation was associated with closer agreement with tape-based measurements in the small subgroup with cranial surface irregularities, while both contour variants performed similarly in examinations without irregularities. These findings are preliminary because of the small cohort, the single tape-based reference measurement per patient, and the 5-case irregularity subgroup. Larger studies using repeated reference measurements and broader cranial morphologies are needed to validate the workflow.
title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging–Based Measurement of Pediatric Head Circumference by a Clinician-in-the-Loop 3D Surface Tool: Development and Validation Study

summary: The tumour microenvironment (TME) is a multidimensional dynamic and complex system of cells and non-cellular components that not only drives tumour progression but also substantially influences response to therapy. Understanding TME biology for basic research and identifying biomarkers in the TME to stratify patients for therapy is crucial for optimizing therapeutic outcomes. Current standards for investigating TME dynamics, if even considered beyond preclinical work, rely predominantly on samples for tissue staining and sequencing and require invasive procedures to obtain tissue via surgery or biopsies. This leads to limited assessment of spatial heterogeneity and minimal temporal information as this depends on the timing of tissue sampling, which results in undefined clinical utility. Molecular imaging provides promising solutions by enabling non-invasive, real-time multidimensional spatiotemporal probing of the TME that can complement current ex vivo practices. This Review highlights the relevance of molecular imaging agents and methods that can effectively capture spatiotemporal TME characteristics in situ, offering critical insights into tumour behaviour and treatment response. We provide an overview of current preclinical imaging strategies and their applications in identifying cellular and non-cellular components of the TME, along with monitoring progression-associated processes and treatment response. We showcase new developments and avenues being explored in preclinical imaging, as well as offer perspectives into existing and emerging clinical imaging of the TME to enhance patient care and highlight opportunities for improvement. Overall, integrating TME imaging into clinical practice holds the potential to bridge critical gaps in spatiotemporal resolution, ultimately enabling more precise diagnosis, patient stratification and personalized therapeutic interventions. This Review discusses molecular imaging probes and modalities for studying the complexity and dynamics of the tumour microenvironment in preclinical research and further highlights emerging clinical applications in diagnostics and intervention.
title: Advances in molecular imaging of the tumour microenvironment

summary: Biophysical whole-brain models may reveal causal links between neural dynamics and biological–environmental variation, yet no framework has explained how these factors become embedded in mechanistic dynamics. Here we develop individualized biophysical digital twins mechanistically linked to phenotypes and expotypes (that is, combinations of exposomal influences) leveraging resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data (n = 6,986, 16 countries) of healthy controls and participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease and frontotemporal dementia. Personalized twins improved goodness-of-fit over group-level models. They reproduced structure–function coupling between regional excitability and brain volume, captured age, sex and neurodegeneration, and encoded 68 expotypes. Associations remained robust after controlling for demographics, data quality, model fit and scanner/site, with the strongest effects for social and physical (pollution) exposomes. We release an open resource (empirical data, code, >3 million simulations) for future research. These findings ground phenotypic–exposomic variation in individualized biophysical twins, enabling in silico testing of mechanisms and potential model-informed interventions. The generation of individual biophysical digital twins at massive scale from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging enables individualized insights into regional signatures and excitatory/inhibitory balance, with features that can be linked to key phenotypes and expotypes.
title: Biophysical brain twins map the phenotype–expotype architecture of ageing and dementia

summary: Background: Tobacco use remains a major global public health challenge, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. China, with the largest smoking population worldwide, faces additional challenges in smoking cessation due to sociocultural factors such as limited depth of risk awareness and strong social norms supporting smoking. Mobile health (mHealth) interventions, particularly smoking cessation apps, offer scalable and accessible support for behavior change. Limited qualitative research explores how Chinese smokers perceive smoking cessation apps and their roles in supporting quitting. Objective: This study aims to explore Chinese smokers’ experience of using smoking cessation apps to support smoking cessation. Methods: Chinese smokers with experience using smoking cessation apps were recruited via purposive sampling through social media. In total, 24 semistructured interviews were conducted online in Mandarin, audio-recorded, and transcribed verbatim. Interview questions explored participants’ experiences of using smoking cessation apps, including their perceptions of different app features, factors influencing their engagement, and how these features supported or hindered their quit attempts. Qualitative analysis was conducted to identify themes related to participants’ experiences regarding smoking cessation apps. Results: Ten themes were identified through qualitative analysis. Smoking cessation apps were perceived as most effective for users who were motivated to quit and believed in the usefulness of the apps. Features such as progress tracking and feedback enhanced extrinsic motivation and self-efficacy, with potential to foster intrinsic motivation over time. However, engagement with apps could decrease as users became more confident in maintaining abstinence. Social support functions provided emotional and informational support, and interactions with other quitters generated positive competition, particularly for users experiencing social isolation, although engagement with these features varied. Relapse prevention components, such as withdrawal symptoms education and recording features, were infrequently used when support was perceived as generic, low intensity, or insufficiently actionable. Good usability and user experience design were key drivers of sustained engagement. Participants valued apps that were simple and intuitive while offering different content formats, although preferences varied between users. Participants also described generic and nonpersonalized support as a limitation, despite rarely explicitly requesting greater personalization. Conclusions: Smoking cessation apps may support quitting through multiple mechanisms, including enhancing motivation and self-efficacy and facilitating social support, but their perceived value and use depend on users’ needs, beliefs, and contexts. The findings highlight broader considerations for mHealth intervention design and evaluation, including interpreting engagement in relation to changing support needs, recognizing that social features may generate additional motivational mechanisms through peer interaction, providing actionable and responsive behavioral support, accommodating diverse user preferences while maintaining usability, and using co-design to identify underlying user needs that may not be explicitly articulated. These considerations may inform the development of more responsive and user-centered mHealth interventions for smoking cessation and other behavior change contexts.
title: Chinese Smokers’ Perspectives on Smoking Cessation Apps: Qualitative Descriptive Study

summary: <strong>Background:</strong> Retrieval over clinical free text underpins record search, cohort identification, and retrieval-augmented language systems. Performance is usually summarized by a single corpus-level mean, which can obscure systematic heterogeneity across patients. <strong>Objective:</strong> This study tests whether known-item retrieval performance varies across an early acute physiological derangement composite measured independently of the text, whether it reproduces under a validated severity-of-illness score, and whether it is robust to alternative outcome, retrieval, and explanatory specifications. <strong>Methods:</strong> We linked 4078 MIMIC-IV (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV) discharge summaries to an adult medical intensive care unit (ICU) cohort and built a pooled, length-matched index of 2956 documents drawn equally from 4 strata of a prespecified composite of early acute physiological derangement, comprising vital signs and Glasgow Coma Scale, mechanical ventilation, and age. A held-out 2-sentence passage had to retrieve its originating summary after removal. Eight contrastively trained dense retrievers, 5 masked language model controls, and BM25 were evaluated. Reciprocal rank at 10 (RR@10) was regressed on exposure stratum with patient-clustered SEs and Holm correction. The analysis was repeated under the Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score (OASIS), a validated first-day score. Additional analyses examined categorical exposure shape, untruncated target rank, hit@10 (hit at 10), lexical representation, query characteristics, age removal, organ dysfunction, and measured covariates. <strong>Results:</strong> Mean RR@10 across dense retrievers fell from 0.127 to 0.080 between the lowest and highest composite stratum (−0.047; mean relative decline 37.2%), with Holm-significant negative slopes in all 8; a pooled model gave −0.0145 per stratum (95% CI −0.0207 to −0.0082; <i>P</i><.001; 23,648 observations). Under OASIS, it fell from 0.127 to 0.078 (−0.049; mean relative decline 38.7%); again, 8 of 8 were Holm-significant. The geometric mean rank of the correct document worsened by a factor of 1.17 per stratum under the composite and 1.24 under OASIS, 8 of 8 significant. BM25 also deteriorated, although from a higher baseline. It persisted across alternative query, indexing, rank, and hit@10 specifications; joint covariate adjustment attenuated the mean coefficient by 21.6%. Removing age attenuated but did not eliminate the pattern: all 8 retained negative slopes, the mean decline fell to 29.7%, and 3 of 8 remained Holm-significant. <strong>Conclusions:</strong> Clinical free-text retrievability declined systematically with worsening early acute physiological derangement. The association held under an externally defined and validated severity-of-illness score as well as the study-specific composite and in lexical as well as dense retrieval. Corpus-level averages can therefore conceal clinically ordered heterogeneity, and clinical retrieval systems should be evaluated across patient strata rather than overall performance alone.
title: Clinical Free-Text Retrieval Across an Acute Physiological Derangement Composite in Intensive Care Unit Discharge Summaries: Stratified Evaluation Study

summary: Background: Patients with traumatic injuries present with heterogeneous injury patterns that are difficult to represent in statistical models. Common approaches either retain individual injury codes in high-dimensional sparse representations, such as one-hot encoding, or aggregate injuries into summary scores, reducing dimensionality at the cost of patient-specific detail. Objective: This study aimed to develop low-dimensional data-driven ICD-10 embeddings for traumatic injuries and compare their downstream discriminatory performance with one-hot encoding of the same injury codes. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study using National Trauma Data Bank (NTDB) records from 2018 and 2019. International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification diagnoses were mapped to World Health Organization ICD-10 codes, retaining traumatic-injury codes S00-S99 and T15-T34. A denoising autoencoder was developed on 2018 data and temporally evaluated on 2019 data. Representations with 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64 dimensions were compared with one-hot encoding across 16 downstream tasks using logistic regression and LightGBM. Performance was measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for binary tasks and macro one-vs-rest AUC for multiclass tasks. Models were trained and evaluated within individual hospitals and separately on the full NTDB. Hospitals were stratified into volume categories, from small (≤500) to major (2500 patients/year). CIs were obtained from 1000 nonparametric bootstrap samples. Results: The development cohort included 1,041,021 eligible patients from 2018, and the temporal evaluation cohort included 1,094,933 patients from 2019. At the hospital level, embeddings outperformed one-hot encoding. With LightGBM at 16 dimensions, the mean paired AUC difference across tasks was 0.054 (95% CI 0.048-0.060) in small hospitals (n=120) vs 0.023 (95% CI 0.020-0.025) in major hospitals (n=99). With logistic regression, differences were 0.056 (95% CI 0.050-0.063) and 0.041 (95% CI 0.039-0.043), respectively. In the full NTDB, 803-indicator one-hot encoding outperformed embeddings. Mean differences were –0.004 (95% CI –0.004 to –0.003) with LightGBM and –0.030 (95% CI –0.030 to –0.029) with logistic regression. At 64 dimensions, these differences narrowed to –0.001 and –0.016, respectively. Conclusions: Embeddings with as few as 8 dimensions achieved predictive performance comparable to or better than one-hot encoding, with up to a 100-fold reduction in dimensionality. Compared to one-hot encoding, embeddings improved performance in models trained at individual hospitals, particularly lower-volume hospitals. These gains may reflect reduced dimensionality, parameter sharing across codes, and representation of codes absent from hospital-specific training data, enabled by embeddings learned from the larger development cohort. In models trained on the full registry, one-hot encoding achieved higher mean AUC with both estimators, although the differences were minor (<0.005 AUC difference) for LightGBM with 16- to 64-dimensional embeddings. The embeddings and software are openly available.
title: Development and Evaluation of Embeddings for Representing Injuries in Patients With Traumatic Injuries: Retrospective Cohort Study

summary:
Importance

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is defined as left ventricular hypertrophy of greater than 15 mm in any part of the left ventricular wall in the absence of valvular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or other chronic conditions causing severe left ventricular hypertrophy such as uncontrolled hypertension or cardiac amyloidosis. Most people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a normal lifespan; however, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with a 0.8% annual incidence of sudden cardiac death.

Observations

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy affects an estimated 0.2% of people worldwide (including more than 600 000 people in the US) and is typically diagnosed with echocardiography. Approximately 35% to 40% of patients report effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Approximately 30% to 40% of people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a pathogenic gene variant that encodes for cardiac sarcomere proteins (predominantly myosin binding protein C, myosin heavy chain, and troponin). Other patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may have a polygenic predisposition and/or nongenetic risk factors. The sarcomeric gene variants cause hypercontractility and delayed relaxation of the cardiac sarcomere, which characterizes the underlying pathophysiologic problem in people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Approximately 60% to 70% of patients have obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, characterized by dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to basal septal hypertrophy. The remainder do not have outflow tract obstruction and, therefore, have nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy should participate in regular low- to moderate-intensity physical activity (such as brisk walking, jogging) as part of a healthy lifestyle. Medical therapies such as β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) and nondihydropyridine-class calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil or diltiazem) are first-line medical therapy for patients with symptoms due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. If first-line therapies do not relieve symptoms, alternative treatments include disopyramide, which improves symptoms in approximately 60% of patients, cardiac myosin inhibitors (mavacamten or aficamten), which improve symptoms in approximately 70% to 80% of patients, or procedures to thin the septal wall of the left ventricle, including percutaneous alcohol septal ablation, which improves symptoms in approximately 75% to 80% of patients, or surgical septal myectomy, which improves symptoms in approximately 90% to 95% of patients. Guidelines recommend that first-degree relatives of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy undergo screening for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with genetic testing or echocardiography.

Conclusions

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is caused by a monogenetic pathogenic variant in approximately 30% to 40% of patients and can cause effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with an incidence of sudden cardiac death of 0.8% per year. First-line therapies for symptomatic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil, diltiazem).
title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Review.

summary: Background: Hospital clinical data warehouses (CDWs) contain longitudinal patient-level information distributed across heterogeneous clinical domains and require strict governance, privacy protection, and controlled data access. Although disease-specific registries facilitate structured clinical research, routine hospital CDW workflows often require repeated technical intervention when clinicians iteratively refine cohorts or integrate additional variables. At Samsung Medical Center (Seoul, Republic of Korea), an operational audit revealed a mean turnaround time of 2.7 (SD 1.6) weeks for clinical data extraction requests, highlighting a workflow gap between clinicians’ research questions and engineer-mediated database query development. Objective: This study describes the development and single-center implementation of IDEA (intersection, difference, expansion, attribution), an informatics abstraction framework designed to support authorized clinicians in performing iterative cohort construction and variable integration within a governed hospital CDW. Methods: IDEA implements 4 user-facing operations: intersection (I), difference (D), expansion (E), and attribution (A). Attribution enables dynamic integration of variables from multiple predefined clinical data domains into an active cohort. IDEA was implemented within the Samsung Medical Center CDW, containing longitudinal electronic health records from 1995 to 2025 and 12 cancer registries. The implementation was evaluated using oncology cross-registry scenarios, descriptive analysis of user actions recorded between January 2024 and December 2025, including 11,460 IDEA operator events, and analysis of 349 user-defined cohorts (“My Registries”) established from 2022 to 2025. Results: IDEA supported interactive cohort construction, refinement, and attribute-based stratification across 12 cancer registries without manual SQL authoring. Clinical end users generated the majority of the 11,460 operator interactions: research nurses accounted for 7918 (69.1%), physicians for 2871 (25.1%), and IT personnel for 619 (5.4%). Attribution was the most frequent operation (8726, 76.1%), suggesting that iterative variable integration into established cohorts was a major use case. Additionally, 349 user-defined cohorts were registered as reusable baseline populations for subsequent cohort curation. Conclusions: IDEA serves as a complementary pathway for clinician-led data curation within a governed hospital CDW, integrating cohort refinement, variable integration, and reusable cohort management into a single workflow. This approach may support selected routine curation tasks for authorized users working with quality-validated data, while complex requests continue to require analyst support. Multicenter evaluations are needed to independently assess dataset accuracy, completeness, and institutional transferability.
title: The IDEA Framework for Clinician-Led Data Curation in a Hospital Clinical Data Warehouse: Single-Center Implementation Study

summary: Abnormal body composition at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with worse survival, but it is rarely measured in practice because manual CT analysis is labor-intensive. We conducted a secondary analysis of a single-center prospective cohort of 509 patients who underwent chest CT within 24 h of ICU admission, of whom 475 were included in the final analysis. Open-source AI segmentation was used to quantify body composition, and the resulting features were related to 6-month survival. Risk scores derived from body composition were significantly associated with 6-month survival (p < 0.001, log-rank test). In five-fold cross-validation, the AUC for discriminating survivors from non-survivors was 0.73; when feature selection was accounted for, the AUC was 0.68 by nested cross-validation and 0.69 by bootstrap optimism correction. The study shows that the automated AI-based analysis of admission chest CT yields body composition scores significantly associated with 6-month mortality after ICU admission.
title: AI-assisted chest CT scan analysis of body composition at ICU admission and 6-month mortality

summary: Background: Dietary habits are strongly associated with a wide range of health outcomes. Although professional interventions are effective, they are resource-intensive. Digital health apps provide a low-cost alternative, and accumulating evidence suggests their potential to improve health behaviors and outcomes. In Japan, some apps are covered by public health insurance; however, evidence from real-world use, particularly regarding both health outcomes and health care expenditures, remains limited. Objective: This study aims to examine the relationship between the use of an automated diet management app and individual health outcomes, as well as health care expenditures, with a particular focus on the frequency of dietary self-monitoring behavior. Using real-world data from Japanese employees in a corporate setting, the study also seeks to provide evidence on the potential economic implications of digital health interventions and to provide evidence relevant to potential behavioral mechanisms underlying their effectiveness. Methods: We constructed individual-level panel data (2021‐2022) by linking app usage records, health checkup records, and medical claims records obtained through a health insurance association in a large Japanese corporate group. The main explanatory variable was the average number of daily meal records over the 90 days preceding the health checkup. We estimated the associations using fixed-effects panel models to control for time-invariant unobserved individual characteristics. Subgroup analyses by sex, age group, and baseline metabolic status were conducted to explore heterogeneity. Linear quantile regression was used as a supplementary analysis. Results: More frequent use of the app was associated with a lower BMI among men (β=−0.126 kg/m², 95% CI −0.22 to −0.04; =.001) and among women (β=−0.372 kg/m², 95% CI −0.54 to −0.20; =.001). Among men, app use was also associated with improvements in waist circumference, blood pressure, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, whereas among women, it was associated with lower probabilities of metabolic syndrome and abnormal blood glucose. Associations with BMI were stronger among users aged ≤40 years and those with poorer baseline health. In contrast, among users aged ≥50 years, improvements were observed primarily in cardiometabolic risk factors rather than BMI. No statistically significant association was observed for short-term health care expenditures. Sensitivity analyses yielded generally consistent findings for the primary outcomes. Conclusions: The findings suggest that digital diet management apps may contribute to statistically significant but modest improvements in health outcomes in workplace settings. However, given the observational nature of the study, the results should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. summary: Background: During the COVID-19 pandemic, older adults living in geriatric care facilities were especially limited in their social interactions because of their vulnerability. Care homes often preferred broad isolation measures to avoid the risk of infection among residents. Digital contact tracing systems (DCTS) developed during the COVID-19 pandemic have the potential to overcome the practice of general isolation in geriatric care facilities, but a prerequisite for their successful implementation is acceptance among nursing staff. Objective: This study aimed to investigate nursing staff’s acceptance of such wearable devices for use within geriatric care facilities and the conditions the technology must meet to increase the likelihood of nursing staff’s acceptance, based on a scenario-based prototype for a digital, wearable-based contact tracing system. Methods: The study used a sequential mixed methods design. Initially, an exploratory literature review provided the foundation for conceptualizing the prototype for the contact tracing system. In the next step, focus groups were conducted among nursing staff with and without prior experience with digital contact tracing at work. Building on those results, a survey study on the prototype’s acceptance was conducted among nursing staff in Germany. The focus group interviews, as well as the survey study, were based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). Results: Based on the few studies that focused on nursing staff’s acceptance of digital contact tracing in medical occupations and the results of the focus group interviews, the scenario-based prototype was developed as a wearable with varying characteristics for nursing staff and residents of geriatric care facilities. The prototype was evaluated as generally favorable by the nursing staff participating in the survey study (n=329), specifically under high-threat pandemic preparedness conditions. Furthermore, the survey study indicates that nursing staff’s intention to use the wearable-based contact tracing system was significantly associated with performance expectancy (β=0.291; <.001), as well as choice of wearable (β=0.174; <.001), and usefulness under threatening conditions (β=0.251; <.001). Extending the UTAUT model by context-specific predictors explained 51.6% (=0.516; = 50.973; <.001; Bonferroni-Holm [BH] corrected =.001×6=.006) of the variance in the intention to use DCTS in geriatric care facilities. This marks a significant increase of explained variance of 7% (=0.074; Δ=16.699; <.001) in comparison to the standard UTAUT model (²=0.446; = 66.954; <.001; BH-corrected =<.001). Conclusions: Nursing staff perceived the proposed scenario-based prototype of a DCTS to be especially useful when no other protective measures, such as vaccines or tests, are available, which is a highly probable scenario. Therefore, preparedness strategies should consider digital contact tracing as one potential component of future pandemic preparedness. Trial Registration: OSF Registries osf.io/82TVA; https://osf.io/82tva
title: Development and Acceptance Evaluation of a Scenario-Based Prototype of a Digital Contact Tracing System in Geriatric Care Facilities: Results From an Exploratory Literature Review, Focus Groups, and a Survey Study

summary: Background: Postpartum hemorrhage is the leading direct cause of maternal mortality worldwide. In rural regions where obstetric clinics lack on-site transfusion capability, distance to the tertiary blood bank is a modifiable determinant of outcome. Existing electronic blood-ordering systems are confined to single-site hospital deployments; no peer-reviewed report describes an interinstitutional perinatal blood dispatch platform coordinating a tertiary blood bank with primary obstetric clinics. Objective: This study aims to describe the design, implementation, and RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance) evaluation of a digital platform linking a tertiary blood bank with 4 community obstetric clinics in rural Taiwan over 4 years. Methods: We conducted an observational implementation evaluation at a tertiary referral center. Launched on November 1, 2021, the platform is a stand-alone web application coordinating ordering, identity and blood-type verification, and cold-chain dispatch across the blood bank and 4 affiliated clinics; it is not electronically integrated with the hospital blood-bank information system. Effectiveness was assessed against 2 prespecified service-level agreement (SLA) targets set by consensus before launch: routine dispatch ≥90% within 90 minutes and emergency dispatch ≥90% within 30 minutes. Reach, adoption, implementation, and maintenance were extracted from platform audit logs. Stakeholder satisfaction was measured using a 28-item service quality (SERVQUAL) instrument at 3 and 15 months postimplementation (clinic physicians, nurses, and allied staff). A continuous-improvement unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) delivery feasibility substudy (initiated in year 3) evaluated whole-blood stability across 4 red-cell storage time points over a 4-km corridor. Results: The platform supported 252 dispatch episodes (38 emergency and 214 routine) from November 1, 2021, through August 31, 2026, and delivered 554 blood product units. Adoption reached 100% (4/4) of eligible clinics and all obstetric clinicians. The emergency SLA was met in 84.2% (32/38) of episodes and 100% in both 2025 and 2026 to date; median emergency turnaround was 28 (IQR 23-29) minutes. The routine SLA was met in 97.7% (209/214) of episodes; median routine turnaround was 72 (IQR 62-79) minutes. Zero serious transfusion-related adverse events were documented across all 252 episodes. SERVQUAL composite satisfaction rose from 4.65 (SD 0.53; n=32; Cronbach α=0.985) at 3 months to 5.00 (SD 0.01; n=38; α uninformative owing to ceiling effect) at 15 months. In the UAV substudy, preflight and postflight whole-blood parameters remained within similar ranges across all 4 storage days. Conclusions: An interinstitutional perinatal blood dispatch platform achieved universal clinic adoption, sustained prespecified SLA targets for emergency and routine dispatch, and was compatible with 0 serious transfusion-related adverse events across nearly 5 years of rural operation. Organizational-level digital health interventions in resource-constrained perinatal networks need not depend on full hospital-information-system integration while supporting sustained service quality; prespecified SLA frameworks plus audit-log analytics offer a transparent evaluation mechanism where randomized comparator designs are infeasible. UAV-delivery feasibility findings are preliminary.
title: Digital Health Platform for Interinstitutional Perinatal Blood Dispatch in Rural Taiwan: 4-Year Implementation Study Using the RE-AIM Framework

summary: Background: Emergency departments (EDs) depend on rapid, reliable triage for patient safety and flow. The Manchester Triage System (MTS) is widely implemented but exhibits known interrater variability. Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as potential decision-support tools for triage and early assessment, yet real-world comparative evaluations remain scarce. Objective: This study aimed to compare clinician and LLM performance on ED triage accuracy, specialty assignment, diagnostic recommendations, and admission prediction in a real-world cohort. Methods: In a retrospective cohort study, 305 walk-in ED encounters at a German tertiary-care hospital were analyzed. A nurse performed real-time MTS-assessment and initial specialty assignment at presentation. Each anonymized case was independently evaluated by 4 physicians and 12 LLMs from 4 providers (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Mistral). Triage agreement was assessed against 2 reference standards: a consensus human label (ground-truth 1 [GT1]) and real-time nurse-assigned MTS-triage (ground-truth 2 [GT2]). For human raters, a leave-one-out variant of GT1 (LOO-GT1) assessed incorporation bias. The primary statistic was quadratic-weighted Cohen κ (unweighted κ reported alongside). Secondary outcomes were directional triage errors (over- or undertriage, |Δ|≤1), specialty top-1 accuracy, per-case precision, recall, -score of recommended diagnostics, and admission prediction (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value [PPV], and negative predictive value [NPV]). Results: Median age was 45 (IQR 31‐62) years; 188 (61.6%) patients were male; admission rate was 20.1% (56/278). Against GT1, human-rater (physicians and nurse) accuracy ranged 0.59‐0.83 (quadratic-weighted κ 0.60‐0.88; unweighted κ 0.35‐0.74), and LLM accuracy 0.35‐0.70 (quadratic-weighted κ 0.46‐0.72; unweighted κ 0.11‐0.53). Under LOO-GT1, human-rater weighted κ fell to 0.48‐0.81. Only 1 clinician (Doctor 1, weighted κ 0.81) retained agreement clearly above any LLM, while 3 LLMs (Gemini-3.5-flash=0.72, GPT-5.5=0.69, and GPT-5=0.66) exceeded the LOO-corrected agreement of the remaining 4 human raters. One-off agreement exceeded 86% for all raters and models. Vs GT1, overtriage ranged 6%‐56% and undertriage 6%‐36%. Vs GT2, corresponding ranges were 11%‐62% and 5%‐30%. Against the study specialty reference, physician specialty-assignment accuracy ranged 0.88‐0.93 and LLM accuracy 0.62‐0.80. Against the operational triage-pathway specialty assignment, the corresponding ranges were 0.81‐0.82 and 0.57‐0.75. Model diagnostic recommendation -scores ranged 0.55‐0.69. Admission prediction demonstrated high sensitivity (0.73‐0.95) and NPV (0.90‐0.96), but modest PPV (0.25‐0.41). Conclusions: In a real-world ED cohort, 1 clinician (Doctor 1, a specialist physician) had the highest urgency agreement point estimate under both GT1 and LOO-GT1. Under LOO-GT1, 3 contemporary LLMs reached agreement that exceeded that of the other 4 clinicians. For specialty assignment, all clinicians remained clearly ahead of the best LLM. LLMs showed strong sensitivity and high NPV for admission prediction, but modest PPV precludes autonomous use. Because both reference standards are empirical rather than outcome-anchored gold standards, findings represent agreement against expert consensus and routine practice rather than an absolute correctness benchmark, and support a complementary, human-in-the-loop role for LLM-based decision-support in ED triage and early assessment.
title: Evaluating Human and AI-Based Triage Performance in the Emergency Department: Real-World Cohort Study

summary: Background: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating virtual patients for health care applications. However, whether LLM-generated virtual patients can reproduce patient-reported priority rankings remains uncertain. Objective: We evaluated whether LLM-generated virtual hypertension patients could approximate real patient-reported perspectives, and whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improved alignment with patient-reported priority rankings. Methods: A total of 20 patients from multiple regions completed structured questionnaires ranking priorities across 7 domains related to AI-assisted hypertension management. A total of 8 LLMs were evaluated under 3 simulation conditions: unconstrained generation, patient-specific simulation, and RAG-enhanced simulation. For unconstrained generation, each model produced 20 virtual patient profiles, each constructed by grouping baseline variables into the study categories and selecting the most frequent category across 10 repeated generations. For patient-specific baseline and RAG-enhanced simulations, each model generated 10 complete questionnaire responses per participant and condition; the modal complete 4-item ranking within each domain was selected as the final ranking. Model-generated rankings were compared with patient-reported rankings using total accuracy, top-1 accuracy, and full accuracy. In addition, 5 hypertension clinicians independently inferred patient-priority rankings while blinded to both real patient responses and LLM outputs, providing a human reference benchmark. Results: Aggregated unconstrained virtual patient profiles varied across models, with 45%‐55% having college-level education, and 75%‐95% using antihypertensive medication. In patient-specific baseline simulations, total accuracy ranged from 46.3% to 71.4%. RAG improved all 3 accuracy metrics across the eight models, increasing mean total accuracy from 62.8% to 76.6%, top-1 accuracy from 51.6% to 72.9%, and full accuracy from 22.2% to 49.4% (all <.001). The largest mean domain-level gains occurred in safety escalation awareness and emotional support and reassurance. Qwen-RAG achieved the highest total accuracy (86.1%) and full accuracy (64.3%). In descriptive comparisons, its corresponding values exceeded those of the clinician consensus (72.5% and 45.0%), while top-1 accuracy was numerically similar (80.7% vs 80.0%). Conclusions: LLM-generated virtual hypertension patients can moderately approximate real patient perspectives, but unconstrained aggregated profiles differed demographically, behaviorally, and clinically from the enrolled reference cohort under the study conditions. RAG substantially improves concordance between virtual patient rankings and patient-reported priorities and may provide a scalable methodological approach for incorporating patient-perspective proxies into digital health research contexts. Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2500102798; https://tinyurl.com/2vahxsed
title: Evaluating Large Language Model–Generated Virtual Hypertension Patients as Proxies for Real Patient Perspectives: Comparative Study

summary: AI-driven clinical decision support systems can prepare executable orders, communicate with patients, and initiate multistep workflows, raising unresolved questions about delegated clinical authority. This viewpoint proposes a 5-level clinical autonomy gradient: informational support (A0), advisory decision support (A1), human-confirmed execution (A2), bounded delegated action (A3), and adaptive autonomous management (A4). Classification applies to a task-action pair within its deployment workflow. Execution authority and case-specific human authorization anchor assignment; decision influence, temporal reach, and scope adaptability describe the configuration. The action-enablement boundary (A1-A2) introduces executable action preparation requiring explicit, informed, case-specific authorization before release. The delegation boundary (A2-A3) permits execution without contemporaneous, case-specific authorization. We adapt an automation scope of practice to record permissions and operating conditions, and an autonomy safety case to link authority to deployment-specific evidence and residual risks. Proposed controls address effective human review, interacting systems, proportionate governance, and withholding, downgrading, or suspending actions when supporting conditions fail. Applications to documented systems and hypothetical scenarios illustrate classification reasoning without establishing reliability or delegated-action safety. Greater autonomy is optional; A1 or A2 may remain appropriate. Independent evaluation must assess classification agreement, feasibility, implementation burden, and effects on care.

summary: Traditional preimplantation genetic testing for in vitro fertilization (IVF) requires invasive trophectoderm biopsy, which may harm the embryo. Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) utilizing cell-free DNA from spent embryo culture medium (SCM) has been attempted, but trace DNA content, maternal cell contamination and high allele drop-out rates are barriers. Here we report an niPGT methodology achieving high diagnostic accuracy among reportable samples across diverse embryo and disease contexts. Reengineered linear whole-genome amplification (scm-LIANTI) with an extremely low error rate is followed by application of a Bayesian algorithm designed to determine which parental haplotypes are inherited at disease-causing sites. Among 191 SCM samples from 29 families affected by rare monogenic disorders, our method amplified all samples and enabled diagnosis of 220 out of 277 pathogenic alleles. All diagnoses (220/220) were concordant with invasive biopsy control. For select embryos, personalized genome-wide genotyping enabled exploratory polygenic risk assessment for type 2 diabetes. Our methodology requires no modification to IVF workflows and represents a key technological advance towards scalable, accurate and safe niPGT for both monogenic and polygenic diseases. A reengineered linear whole-genome amplification approach combined with Bayesian linkage analysis enables highly accurate non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing of embryos from families with rare monogenic disorders.
title: Highly accurate non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic and polygenic diseases from spent medium

summary:
Background

The current less intensive guidelines for pulmonary nodule follow-up have not been compared with more intensive strategies.

Objective

To determine whether less intensive follow-up of small pulmonary nodules is noninferior to more intensive follow-up.

Design

Unblinded, cluster randomized, pragmatic comparative effectiveness trial. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02623712).

Setting

24 clusters of U.S. hospitals and health care systems.

Participants

34 686 patients with a new pulmonary nodule measuring 15 mm or less, detected incidentally or by screening.

Intervention

Follow-up protocols were modeled on current and prior recommendations from the Fleischner Society and the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS). Each cluster was randomly assigned to the less or more intensive follow-up protocol.

Measurements

The primary outcome was the proportion of lung cancers measuring more than 20 mm at diagnosis. Analyses were conducted using mixed-effects logistic regression. The prespecified noninferiority margin was 5 percentage points.

Results

A total of 34 686 participants (50.8% women) were enrolled, with a mean age of 64.5 years (SD, 11.7). Lung cancer was diagnosed within 27 months of nodule identification in 273 of 17 841 participants (1.5%) in the less intensive group and 231 of 16 845 (1.4%) in the more intensive group. Among participants with lung cancer with available data, 97 of 267 (36.3%) in the less intensive group and 62 of 224 (27.7%) in the more intensive group had cancers larger than 20 mm at diagnosis. After adjustment, more lung cancers larger than 20 mm were identified with less intensive screening (7 percentage points [95% CI, -2.0 to 15.9 percentage points]), exceeding the noninferiority margin but not statistically significant.

Limitations

Suboptimal adherence, limited power, and residual confounding.

Conclusion

Small, malignant pulmonary nodules frequently progress during follow-up. Although neither follow-up strategy was clearly superior, these data raise concerns about the less intensive recommendations for follow-up of small nodules.

Primary funding source

Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute.
title: Less Versus More Intensive Strategies for Follow-up of Small Pulmonary Nodules : A Cluster Randomized Pragmatic Clinical Trial.

summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) lacks scalable and mechanism-informed computational strategies for prioritizing repurposable drug combinations. Here, we developed FeNetDP, a multimodal AI-guided framework that integrates transcriptomic, proteomic, single-cell, spatial, and clinical survival data to enable biologically grounded drug repurposing and combination prioritization in PDAC. FeNetDP combines gene-level network proximity analysis with a biologically constrained neural ranking model to identify candidate compounds and drug pairs linked to a disease-relevant ferroptosis suppressor program. Using this framework, we defined an eight-gene ferroptosis suppressor module enriched in ductal cells and associated with poor prognosis, and prioritized candidate repurposable compounds and combinations targeting this network state. Prospective experimental validation identified panobinostat plus sorafenib as a synergistic combination that suppresses tumor growth and promotes ferroptosis in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, the combination impaired ferroptosis resistance through coordinated disruption of glutathione-dependent antioxidant defense and AIFM2 (FSP1)-associated glutathione-independent protection. Together, these findings establish FeNetDP as a multimodal and experimentally grounded framework for computational repurposing and mechanism-informed therapeutic prioritization in cancer.
title: Multimodal AI-enabled repurposing and prioritization of ferroptosis-targeting drug combinations in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma

summary:
Importance

Early resuscitation with intravenous fluids is recommended for patients with sepsis.

Objective

To determine the effect of liberal vs more conservative fluid resuscitation strategies in the ambulance on mortality among patients with suspected sepsis.

Design, setting, and participants

Multicenter, 2 × 2 factorial randomized clinical trial conducted by 4 paramedic services and their destination hospitals in Ontario, Canada. Participants were adults with suspected sepsis, defined as suspected infection, fever (≥38.0 °C), and hypotension (systolic blood pressure [SBP] <100 mm Hg), and obtainable intravenous access. Patients were enrolled between March 23, 2020, and August 20, 2025, with last follow-up in December 2025.

Intervention

Patients were randomized to receive liberal fluids (up to 2 L of normal saline regardless of subsequent SBP) or usual care (fluids only when SBP <90 mm Hg and stopped when SBP ≥100 mm Hg) during prehospital care and until transfer of care in the emergency department. (Patients were additionally randomized to receive ceftriaxone vs placebo; analysis of which is reported separately.).

Main outcomes and measures

The primary outcome was hospital mortality, defined as death prior to hospital discharge up to day 90. There were 17 secondary outcomes, including all-cause mortality at 90 days, hospitalization, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor therapy, dialysis, and total fluids infused within 24 hours of hospital arrival.

Results

Among 1686 randomized patients, 1669 were eligible and 1646 were included in the primary outcome analysis (830 in the liberal fluids group and 816 in the usual fluids group). The median age of patients was 76 (IQR, 63-85) years and 938 (57.0%) were male. Most patients in both groups received a fluid bolus (826/848 [97.4%] in the liberal fluids group; 700/821 [85.3%] in the usual fluids group) during transport, but patients in the liberal fluids group received a larger volume (median, 1500 mL [IQR, 1000-2000 mL]) vs 500 mL [IQR, 175-800 mL] in the usual fluids group; difference, 910.1 mL [95% CI, 857.3-962.9 mL]). Hospital mortality was 149/830 (18.0%) in the liberal fluids group and 149/816 (18.3%) in the usual fluids group (risk ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.80-1.20]; unadjusted risk difference, -0.3 [95% CI, -4.0 to 3.4]; P = .82). Among the 17 secondary outcomes, all were similar between groups. Adverse events, including pulmonary edema during transport, were infrequent in both groups.

Conclusions and relevance

A more liberal fluid resuscitation strategy for the prehospital management of patients with suspected sepsis did not reduce mortality compared with more restrictive usual care.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03068741.
title: Prehospital Fluid Resuscitation for Patients With Suspected Sepsis: The PITSTOP-Fluids Factorial Randomized Clinical Trial.

summary:
Background

Contemporary data on sexual behaviour are needed to inform and evaluate sexual and reproductive health strategies and services and understand societal shifts. In this assessment of the National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal), we aimed to provide up-to-date prevalence estimates and examine changes in key sexual behaviours in Britain reported between 1990 and 2024.

Methods

The Natsal study is repeat cross-sectional probability-sample surveys of the British population, undertaken approximately decennially since 1990. Natsal-4 (2022-24) used interviewer-administered and self-completion questionnaires, among two probability samples: an address-based sample and a probability panel. Data were weighted to broadly align with Britain's sociodemographic structure. In Natsal-4, prevalence of sexual experiences, partner numbers, frequency of sex, and online behaviours are presented by age and gender among participants aged 16-59 years, with changes in prevalence across Natsal surveys presented by age and gender among participants aged 16-44 years.

Findings

Of 6719 Natsal-4 participants (aged 16-59 years), 89·4% (95% CI 88·3-90·4) reported ever having sex (median five lifetime partners for both women and men). In the past year, 77·0% (95% CI 75·6-78·4) reported having had sex, and 65·5% (63·9-67·0) reported one sexual partner. Reporting at least one new partner in the past year was highest among participants aged 16-24 years (21·7% [95% CI 17·3-26·8] in women, 30·1% [24·5-36·4] in men). Pornography use and sexting (sending or receiving sexual images) in the past year were more common among men (80·7% [95% CI 78·6-82·6] and 26·0% [23·9-28·3], respectively) than among women (36·6% [34·7-38·5] and 22·2% [20·5-23·9], respectively); both were higher among younger age groups. The proportion of 16-24-year-olds who reported never having had sex increased from 18·9% (95% CI 17·0-20·9) in Natsal-3 (2010-12) to 37·7% (36·2-43·1) in Natsal-4 (2022-24) among women; and 18·2% (16·2-20·4) to 28·4% (23·1-34·5) among men. Reporting of same-sex sex increased among 16-44-year-olds from 6·8% (95% CI 6·1-7·6) in 2010-12 to 14·0% (12·4-15·7) in 2022-24 among women, and from 4·0% (3·3-4·7) to 12·3% (10·4-14·5) among men. Among 16-44-year-olds, we found a decline in average frequency of sex from four times per month in Natsal-1 (1990) to twice per month in Natsal-4 (2022-24).

Interpretation

Sexual behaviour in Britain has shifted markedly since 1990, including a recent decline in sexual experience among young people and increased reporting of same-sex attraction and behaviour across all age groups. Sexual and reproductive health policies and services remain essential and must adapt to shifting needs and new areas of risk and vulnerability, including safe engagement in online sexual activity.

Funding

Wellcome Trust, the UK Economic and Social Research Council, and the UK National Institute for Health Research.
title: Prevalence and trends in sexual behaviour in Britain from 1990 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal).

summary:
Background

Reducing racial mortality disparities remains a central goal of U.S. health policy, and progress varies by cause of death.

Objective

To quantify cause-specific contributions to changes in excess mortality rate (EMR) among Black versus White populations.

Design

Cross-sectional temporal analyses.

Setting

Mortality data.

Participants

Non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White decedents stratified by sex and age at death (<20, <65, or ≥65 years).

Measurements

EMRs among Black versus White populations in 1993 and 2023 for all-cause and 24 causes of death, calculated as differences in age-standardized mortality rates, and changes in EMRs, calculated by subtracting the 2023 EMR from the 1993 EMR with cause-specific contribution to all-cause EMR reduction, expressed as a percentage.

Results

In 2023, all-cause EMR for Black versus White persons decreased by 56% (288.5 deaths per 100 000 person-years) for males and by 68% (175.8 deaths per 100 000 person-years) for females compared with 1993. Among males, reductions were predominantly driven by cancer (38.2% [95% CI, 36.4% to 40.0%]), HIV (17.5% [CI, 17.0% to 18.1%]), and heart disease (12.3% [CI, 10.2% to 14.4%]); among females, primary drivers were heart disease (31.9% [CI, 29.8% to 34.0%]), cancer (13.0% [CI, 11.3% to 14.8%]), and HIV (7.9% [CI, 7.5% to 8.3%]). Further gains were limited by lower progress or worsening disparities in maternal death; nephritis and accidents and adverse effects in both sexes; and homicide and legal intervention, diabetes, hypertension without heart disease, and cerebrovascular diseases (≥65 years) in males. Over time, cancer fell from the leading contributor to sixth among males and from second to fifth among females, whereas HIV declined from fourth or fifth to tenth in both sexes as contributors to the Black-White mortality gap.

Limitation

The analysis compared 1993 and 2023, although peak EMR years varied by cause of death, and alternative periods could yield different cause-specific contributions.

Conclusion

Reductions in EMR among Black versus White populations were driven by improvements in mortality from major causes. Shifting drivers of the racial mortality gap highlight priorities for further progress.

Primary funding source

American Cancer Society and Research Ireland.
title: Progress in Reducing the Black-White Mortality Gap From 1993 to 2023 in the United States: An Analysis of the National Mortality Database.

summary: Background: Problematic social media use (PSMU) is linked to depression, anxiety, and loneliness, requiring valid measurement tools. The Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS) is the most widely used PSMU measure internationally, but has not been validated in Czech adults. Objective: This study aimed to (1) validate the Czech BSMAS by evaluating structural validity, internal consistency, measurement invariance, and construct validity, and comparing latent-factor and network representations; and (2) evaluate, in a multivariable prediction-modeling framework with an independent replication sample, whether item-level BSMAS scores predict depression, anxiety, and loneliness better than the conventional sum score. Methods: Two independent nonprobability convenience samples of Czech adults were recruited online via snowball sampling (primary: N=3297; replication: N=514). Structural validity was assessed with confirmatory factor analysis; internal consistency with α and ω. Measurement invariance across gender (configural, metric, and scalar) and differential item functioning across age were assessed. Construct validity was explored through Spearman correlations with depression, anxiety, and loneliness (total, emotional, and social). Latent and network models were compared using the Bayesian information criterion (BIC). For prediction, 5 algorithms compared the BSMAS sum score with the 6 individual items as predictors, using repeated 10-fold cross-validation; performance was quantified with out-of-sample and root-mean-square error. The item-level comparison was additionally evaluated with models fixed in the primary sample and applied unchanged to the replication sample, and with sociodemographic characteristics held constant (registered on Open Science Framework: v9emk). Results: A one-factor model fit well (=101.5, <.001; comparative fit index [CFI]=0.993; root-mean-square error of approximation [RMSEA]=0.056) and reproduced in the replication sample. Internal consistency was high (α=0.87; =0.87). Scalar invariance across gender was supported; 2 of 6 items showed differential item functioning across age. Correlations were moderate with depression (ρ=0.31‐0.38) and anxiety (ρ=0.32‐0.45), small with emotional loneliness (ρ=0.28‐0.29), and negligible to small with social loneliness (ρ=0.03‐0.16). The latent model was more parsimonious than the network model (ΔBIC=–59.32). Item-level representation modestly outperformed the sum score for depression (²=0.15 vs 0.10) and anxiety (²=0.16 vs 0.11). This advantage was reproduced in the replication sample, held with models fixed in the primary sample (Δ²=0.069, 90% CI 0.040‐0.100, and 0.067, 90% CI 0.043‐0.093) and after sociodemographic adjustment, and was not accounted for by weighting items by their standardized factor loadings. More flexible algorithms did not outperform linear regression. Loneliness, especially its social dimension, was poorly predicted by BSMAS scores. Conclusions: In these samples, the Czech BSMAS showed a predominantly unidimensional structure and high internal consistency, with scalar invariance across gender but age-related differential item functioning in 2 items. Item-level scoring offered a small, reproducible predictive advantage for depression and anxiety, although absolute predictive performance was low. Replication in representative samples is needed before population-level or clinical application.
title: Psychometric Properties and Predictive Performance of the Czech Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale for Mental Health Outcomes: Validation and Multivariable Modeling Study in an Adult Convenience Sample

summary:
Background

Previous reviews on prostate cancer screening relied on ongoing trials of invitations to screening with prostate-specific antigen (PSA), which may lack sufficient follow-up for mortality and overdiagnosis. Other screening tests with higher specificity may improve the benefit-harm profile.

Purpose

To examine benefits and harms of screening versus no screening or usual care.

Data sources

MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (2014 to 28 January 2026); reviews and included studies for studies published before 2014.

Study selection

Paired reviewers identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective nonrandomized studies. Benefit outcomes relied on data reported by age when possible.

Data extraction

Paired reviewers extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was conducted with investigation of heterogeneity; assessment of certainty of evidence used the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach with decision thresholds as the targets of certainty.

Data synthesis

Thirteen RCTs (n = 792 034; 8 from a multisite European trial, and 1 for harms only) and 3 uncontrolled cohort studies (n = 5593; all for harms) were included. All RCTs compared invitations to PSA-based screening versus no invitation. At 20 years' follow-up, among 1000 men who were invited to multiple rounds of PSA-based screening every 2 to 4 years starting at age 55 to 69 years (mean, 62 years), there was likely a reduction in prostate cancer mortality (≥2 fewer) and metastatic cancer incidence (≥6 fewer) at the expense of prostate cancer overdiagnosis (≥20 cases) and false positives (≥150 cases) (all moderate certainty). Findings for ages 50 to 54 years were less certain. An invitation to 1 round of screening or to start screening at age 70 to 74 years may not lead to important benefit or harm (low to moderate certainty).

Limitation

Findings may differ for populations at elevated risk.

Conclusion

There was low- to very-low-certainty evidence of no important benefit for a 1-time invitation to PSA screening. Moderate-certainty evidence showed benefit with multiple invitations to PSA-based screening starting at age 55 to 69 years, although with harm from overdiagnosis and false positives.

Primary funding source

Public Health Agency of Canada. (PROSPERO: CRD420250651056).
title: Screening for Prostate Cancer : A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

summary:
Background

Sexual wellbeing is an individual state of feeling respected, safe, and comfortable with sex and sexuality, and having self-esteem, agency, and support in one's sexual life. It is related to, but distinct from, sexual function and sexual health. The epidemiology of sexual wellbeing in a general population is not well understood. We aimed to examine inequalities in low sexual wellbeing, and discover associations with sexual behaviour, sexual and reproductive health experiences, and general and mental health. We sought to understand which individual items within our validated 13-item measure of sexual wellbeing (the Natsal-SW) are most strongly associated with key sexual health behaviours and indicators.

Methods

We conducted the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), which is a large nationally representative cross-sectional study of people aged 16-59 years who are resident in Britain (data used here collected between Sept 20, 2022, and Dec 3, 2023). 4160 participants reporting sexual experience ever completed the Natsal-SW; standardised score range 0-52, low selected as ≤33, and high as ≥48. Focusing attention on those with most need, we used age-adjusted logistic regressions to examine associations with low sexual wellbeing.

Findings

The weighted prevalence of current low sexual wellbeing was similar in women (14·3% [95% CI 12·6-16·3]) and men (13·7% [11·7-15·9]), but high sexual wellbeing was slightly less prevalent in women than men (20·7% [95% CI 18·7- 22·8] vs 24·4% [21·8- 27·1]; p=0·024). Nine items on Natsal-SW differed by gender; notably women were more likely to report feeling upset with others about past sexual events, and men to report feeling ashamed about sexual thoughts. The odds of low sexual wellbeing were greater among young people (aged 16-24 years), individuals from sexual and gender minorities, individuals reporting lower income and, among women only, educational level. Low sexual wellbeing was associated with reporting first sex after age 25 years, symptoms of sexually-transmitted infections and less frequent sex in the past month, at least four partners, distressing sexual problems, and sexual violence in the past year, and at least one same-sex partner in the past 5 years. Low sexual wellbeing was associated with currently screening positive for depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-2-item) and anxiety (Generalised Anxiety Disorder-2-item) symptoms and low mental wellbeing, particularly among men. Associations between key sexual health and behaviour indicators, and low sexual wellbeing, remained after adjustment for mental health.

Interpretation

Low sexual wellbeing is unequally distributed, and patterns of association differ notably from sexual health. These data support future inclusion of sexual wellbeing in population health policy and intervention.

Funding

Wellcome Trust, the UK Economic and Social Research Council, and the UK National Institute for Health and Care Research.
title: Sexual wellbeing in Britain: findings from the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4).

summary: Background: The Military Health System mandates medical documentation at all echelons of care; however, care providers in combat situations must prioritize lifesaving measures over record-keeping, leading to information gaps. Effective human-machine teaming solutions designed to autonomously document care delivery will serve as future force multipliers in tactical combat casualty care (TCCC) environments. Objective: This study proposed a standardized performance evaluation framework for AI algorithms designed to passively document care delivery in the TCCC environment. Common AI performance evaluation methods do not adequately represent the temporal, repetitive, and context-dependent nature of real-world TCCC delivery. Comprehensive assessments are necessary to evaluate AI tools in a manner that reflects the longitudinal and workflow-dependent nature of care delivery. Methods: To assess performance, the research team leveraged a reserved dataset. In the first phase of the assessment, a standardized, repeatable performance methodology and framework was used to evaluate individual algorithms that detect (1) treatments administered by the care provider, (2) visible medical objects, and (3) injuries and their localizations. Detection effectiveness included 4 metrics: Jaccard Index, also known as intersection over union, precision, recall, and -score. Processing efficiency was evaluated by lag time scores. The second phase incorporated a centralized orchestration framework to support representative edge-constrained and synchronized execution, as well as computational resource characterization within a workflow-aware environment. In addition, quantified memory consumption and processing unit resource usage were assessed. Results: Results are summarized for a representative algorithm in each category to illustrate the evaluation framework. Medical procedure detection yielded procedure-level mean -scores from 0.00 to 0.31 and simulation-level means from 0.00 to 0.33. Higher mean -scores were observed for nasopharyngeal airway, chest seal application, and treat a casualty for a cold injury (mean =0.28, 0.31, and 0.31, respectively). Medical object detection achieved mean -scores of approximately 0.42 (range 0‐0.71). Injury detection and localization showed mean -scores of approximately 0.27 (range 0‐0.60). These results illustrate the ability of the framework to characterize performance variability across algorithms and simulations. Conclusions: The proposed evaluation framework provides standardized, workflow-aware assessment of AI algorithms for core TCCC documentation tasks. While algorithm performance to date is low, the framework captures performance variability across algorithms and supports targeted identification of underperforming areas for iterative AI model refinement. The framework provides a foundation for broader evaluation of clinical and digital health systems that require event-level reasoning and workflow-aware assessment.
title: Standardized Performance Assessment Methodology and Evaluation Framework for Tactical Combat Casualty Care Autonomous Documentation Algorithms: Framework Development and Evaluation

summary: Extended reality (XR) is increasingly used in rehabilitation but its effectiveness in chronic respiratory conditions remains unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental studies comparing XR-based interventions with usual care or alternatives. Searches were performed from inception to March 2025 and risk of bias was assessed by two independent reviewers. Fifteen experimental studies were included. XR-based interventions significantly improved 6-min walk distance (mean difference [MD] = 29.90 meters), forced vital capacity (MD = 0.37 liters), reduced dyspnea (standardized mean difference [SMD] = −0.61), anxiety (SMD = −2.08), and depression (SMD = −1.10), and improved quality of life (SMD = −1.87). No significant effects were observed for forced expiratory volume in one second percent predicted or fatigue. Subgroup analyses showed stronger effects in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and with comprehensive XR programs. Exercise-based XR improved quality of life only, while activities of daily living simulations improved forced expiratory volume in one second percent predicted, and nature-based interventions showed no significant benefit. Heterogeneity was substantial, but sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of primary outcomes. XR-based rehabilitation may improve exercise capacity, symptoms, and quality of life, but larger multicenter trials are required to confirm long-term effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.
title: A systematic review and meta analysis of extended reality interventions for chronic respiratory conditions

summary: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.
title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis.

summary: Background: Mental health and well-being services generate substantial operational and client-level data. Review-level evidence on how data-driven methods support service delivery remains fragmented across technologies and settings. Objective: This study aimed to synthesize review-level evidence on data-driven methods relevant to mental health and well-being service delivery, including business intelligence (BI), data visualization, and machine learning (ML), and identify applications, implementation challenges, and evidence gaps. Methods: We conducted an umbrella review following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020. The original searches of Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and PsycINFO were completed on January 27, 2026. During revision, supplementary PubMed and Embase searches were conducted on September 22, 2026. For both supplementary databases, the search was restricted at the database-search stage to publications from 2021 to the current date and to review/systematic review records; eligibility screening then retained the original January 27, 2026, evidence cutoff. All records were independently screened by 2 reviewers using Covidence (Veritas Health Innovation); the reviewer pair differed between the original and supplementary search phases. Eight structured reviews were critically appraised using the JBI checklist and synthesized narratively. Results: Eight structured reviews were included (3 systematic reviews, 4 scoping reviews, and 1 umbrella review). Seven reviews contributed primary study or source-level evidence, while one umbrella review synthesized 44 reviews. The retrieved evidence was dominated by AI and ML, including conversational agents, natural language processing, and clinical decision support, whereas dedicated BI and operational data visualization syntheses were sparse. Two reviews directly addressed mental health service delivery, 4 were adjacent or partially direct, and 2 were indirect but relevant. Only one review focused specifically on mental health helplines. Service-level benefits were reported more consistently than sustained clinical benefits, although the evidence remained heterogeneous and partly indirect. Safety and implementation concerns included symptom worsening, bias, hallucination, privacy, trust, integration barriers, and inequitable access. Conclusions: Review-level evidence relevant to mental health and well-being services is uneven and concentrated on AI/ML. Because the search required all 3 concept blocks, BI- and visualization-focused reviews may have been under-retrieved. BI and operational data visualization, helpline-specific implementation, long-term effectiveness, safety, and equity require more direct and prospective evaluation before findings can be generalized across service settings.
