summary: Background: Health-promoting new media can extend access to health information and education in rural communities. However, services need to accommodate residents’ preferences for both communication features and practical requirements for use. Existing research on technology acceptance and disease-specific applications provides limited evidence about how rural residents weigh these features together when choosing services for general health promotion. Understanding these preferences can help guide locally appropriate digital service development. Objective: This study aimed to quantify rural residents’ stated preferences for functional attributes of health-promoting new media, explore preference variation, and identify priorities for services suited to rural community settings. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional discrete choice experiment in 3 townships in Guizhou Province, China, from August to October 2024. Adults with experience using new media were recruited through convenience sampling and completed face-to-face questionnaires. A literature review, expert consultation, and resident focus groups identified 6 attributes: operation mode, device type, information content, experience, information source, and daily time investment. The questionnaire was pretested with 20 residents before the main survey. Investigators provided standardized explanations and visual aids when needed to support comprehension. The experimental design included 24 choice tasks divided into 3 blocks. Each respondent completed 8 tasks, selecting between 2 hypothetical service profiles without an opt-out option. Conditional logit models estimated average preferences using respondent-clustered SEs. We report coefficients and 95% CIs. Daily time investment was modeled categorically, with 1 hour per day as the reference. Mixed logit models explored preference heterogeneity. Participants provided written informed consent. Results: The analysis included 327 respondents who contributed 2616 choice occasions; 247 (75.5%) were women and 208 (63.6%) were aged 41 to 50 years. Most respondents had primary school education or below (n=198, 60.6%) and an annual household income per capita of ≤10,000 RMB (RMB 1=US $0.14035 as of October 31, 2024; n=194, 59.3%). Participants preferred voice or click operation over typing (β=−0.18, 95% CI −0.25 to −0.11), mobile phones over professional devices (β=−0.20, 95% CI −0.28 to −0.13), and basic over personalized content (β=−0.17, 95% CI −0.25 to −0.09). Daily time preferences were nonmonotonic: compared with 1 hour per day, 3 hours per day had lower utility (β=−1.06, 95% CI −1.52 to −0.60), whereas 5 hours per day had higher utility (β=0.25, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.34). Average preferences for experience and information source were not statistically significant. Supplementary mixed logit models yielded similar average preference estimates. Conclusions: Mobile delivery, voice or click operation, and basic health information were preferred features among participants in this study. These findings identify priorities for developing and evaluating health promotion prototypes in comparable communities. The nonmonotonic time pattern requires further investigation, and stated preferences should be evaluated against observed use. Convenience sampling limits the transferability of these findings to other rural populations.

summary: Background: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), defined as the co-occurrence of at least 2 of 3 conditions (diabetes, coronary heart disease, and stroke), is associated with higher mortality than the individual conditions. Lifestyle behaviors, adiposity, and clinical abnormalities are interrelated, but their conditional dependency structure and sex-specific organization remain incompletely understood. Objective: We aimed to characterize sex-specific dependency patterns linking lifestyle factors, adiposity, clinical indicators, and CMM using Bayesian networks (BNs); identify structurally important nodes; and compare BN performance with that of other machine learning models. Methods: We analyzed baseline data from 76,128 adults in the Beijing Health Management Cohort. Within each sex, data were split into training (80%) and held-out test (20%) sets before preprocessing. Imputation, discretization, and feature selection were performed using training data only. Sex-specific BNs were learned using hill climbing with bootstrap arc-strength thresholding and characterized using graph-theoretic metrics. BN predictions were based on the conditional probability table of CMM given its parent nodes. BN performance was compared with that of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), neural network, and random forest models. Sensitivity analyses were performed by varying the arc-strength threshold from 0.40 to 0.85. Results: The male BN included 15 nodes and 39 edges, whereas the female BN was composed of 13 nodes and 26 edges. Age and hypertension were directly connected to CMM in both sexes, whereas a direct connection between high triglyceride levels and CMM was observed only in males. Age had the highest betweenness centrality in males, whereas hypertension ranked highest in females. Body roundness index (BRI) was not directly connected to CMM in either overall network. Its betweenness centrality was below the network mean in males (0.043 vs 0.059) but above the network mean in females (0.138 vs 0.078). In held-out testing, the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the BNs were 0.810 (95% CI 0.782‐0.838) in males and 0.846 (95% CI 0.810‐0.882) in females. The areas under the precision-recall curve were 0.090 and 0.084, respectively, representing 3.6 and 5.6 times the respective prevalence baselines. Mean predicted risks approximated observed prevalence (2.54% vs 2.53% in males and 1.52% vs 1.51% in females), with calibration slopes of 1.11 and 1.03, respectively. BN discrimination was significantly lower than that of XGBoost in both sexes and that of the neural network in females but significantly higher than that of the random forest in both sexes. The principal direct connections to CMM were preserved across all thresholds. Conclusions: Sex-specific BNs characterized conditional associations linking lifestyle, adiposity, and clinical factors with CMM. Age and hypertension showed direct connections to CMM in both sexes, whereas a direct connection between high triglyceride levels and CMM was observed only in males. BRI was not directly connected to CMM in either overall network and showed above-average betweenness in females. Although BNs showed favorable calibration, their discrimination did not exceed that of the strongest comparator models. Given the cross-sectional design, these relationships are associational and require longitudinal confirmation.
title: Lifestyle and Clinical Factors Associated With Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity Among Adults in Beijing: Cross-Sectional Bayesian Network Analysis

summary: Background: Substance use disorders account for a significant portion of the disease burden attributed to mental health globally, but measurement remains suboptimal. Substance use measurement is over-reliant on retrospective recall, often over long periods of time. However, the episodic, contextual, and event- or time-contingent nature of substance use calls into question the validity of these traditional retrospective measurement methods. One method to overcome these limitations is ecological momentary assessment (EMA), which repeatedly samples participant behaviors and experiences in real time, in the context in which they occur. Objective: This review aimed to systematically identify studies using EMA to measure substance use, provide a comprehensive overview of the EMA methods used, and develop a checklist for improving the reporting of methodological information for future EMA studies in this field. Methods: Studies published between 2018 and 2026 were sourced from PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus, and PsycINFO via Ovid databases on March 31, 2026, using terms related to EMA, digital phenotyping, passive sensing, daily diary, and specific terms for each drug type. Studies that actively or passively assessed thoughts and/or behavior in the participants’ natural environment/daily lives, in a repeated manner, at or close to the behavior of interest (substance use), using either automatic prompts or notifications, were included. Studies were not excluded according to populations, age, setting, or study design. This study was preregistered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD42023400418). Results: The search identified 12,487 articles, of which 1236 were reviewed in full; 581 studies were included and extracted, resulting in 431 (n=126,733 participants) unique datasets. Most studies were conducted in the United States (348/431, 80.7%) and focused on alcohol (364/431, 84.5%) and cannabis use (172/431, 39.9%) with or without the presence of other substance use. Alcohol and cannabis measurement co-occurred the most in 128 of 431 (29.7%) unique datasets. Phencyclidine, bath salts, cough syrup, crack, depressants, prescription sedatives, prescription tranquilizers, steroids, khat, buprenorphine, gamma-hydroxybutyrate, kava, and kratom were only measured in one dataset each. This review found limited reporting consistency across compliance, completion windows, attrition rates, survey duration, and data collection technologies in EMA substance use studies. Conclusions: This review provides the first comprehensive cross-substance synthesis of EMA methodologies used to measure substance use. In contrast to previous reviews focused on individual substances or narrower methodological issues, it compares methodological characteristics across substance groups and identifies common design and reporting gaps. The findings provide practical recommendations to improve the transparency, comparability, reproducibility, feasibility, and data quality of future EMA studies. Greater consistency in reporting missing data, compliance, survey duration, and prompt completion windows, alongside further integration of wearable technologies and research on underexplored substances, will be important for strengthening the real-world application of EMA in substance use research.
title: Measuring Substance Use With Ecological Momentary Assessment: Scoping Review of Methods and Key Recommendations for a Methodological and Reporting Framework

summary: Distinguishing Group A streptococcus (GAS) pharyngitis from viral upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) is critical for appropriate antibiotic use but remains difficult on symptoms alone. We developed and internally validated a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model fusing pharyngeal images (Swin Transformer) with clinical metadata via gradient boosting decision trees, using 6666 visits and 119,988 images from 44 facilities collected March 2023–August 2025. For discriminating GAS from non-GAS (influenza A/B, COVID-19), the fusion model achieved area under the curve (AUC) 0.917 (95% confidence interval 0.907–0.926), outperforming image-only (0.902), metadata-only (0.871) and proxy Centor/McIsaac scores. At a pre-specified high-specificity threshold (≥0.90) sensitivity was 0.761; simulations indicated antibiotic-prescription reductions of 23–56% across GAS prevalences of 5–20%. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed.
title: Multimodal AI for bacterial vs viral upper respiratory tract infection multicentre development and internal validation

summary: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), formerly known as myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries, challenges the long-standing assumption that myocardial infarction is synonymous with obstructive coronary artery disease. Rather than a paradox, MINOCA reflects the limitations of angiography-centred paradigms and the complexity of contemporary cardiovascular pathophysiology. Consistent with this updated definition, this Review approaches MINOCA as a working diagnosis that encompasses diverse mechanisms, including plaque disruption, coronary vasomotor dysfunction, microvascular disease, and non-coronary conditions. We propose a pragmatic, mechanism-oriented framework for selecting and sequencing complementary investigations, highlighting how intracoronary imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, and coronary functional testing can be integrated according to the clinical scenario to refine diagnosis, while balancing diagnostic yield with procedural risk and resource availability. We discuss the implications for management, emphasising that treatment should be guided by underlying pathophysiology rather than a uniform approach derived from obstructive myocardial infarction. Emerging evidence supports the implementation of a stratified therapy to improve patient-centred outcomes. Finally, we discuss research priorities for improving mechanism-specific diagnosis and treatment, arguing that MINOCA represents both a conceptual advance and a transitional step toward a mechanism-based taxonomy of myocardial injury and infarction.
title: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries: diagnostic pathways and stratified treatment.

summary: Providing targeted, quality-assured patient information is essential for informed and autonomous decision-making but remains resource-intensive when delivered face-to-face. Multimedia-supported informed consent may enhance patient understanding and satisfaction while reducing physician time by complementing, rather than replacing, direct interaction. Our PRISMA-based systematic review, aiming to enable clinicians to implement and evaluate such a supplement, identified 907 articles of which 110 reports from OECD countries were included, including 62 randomized controlled trials. Among studies assessing the outcomes of interest, 71% reported improved patient understanding with multimedia tools compared to standard consent, 41% reported increased patient satisfaction (none reported decreases), and 91% found reduced or unchanged patient anxiety. In synthesis, to the extent possible despite substantial heterogeneity, findings suggest benefits and potential efficiency gains, and we were able to derive recommendations. However, considerable methodological variability and limitations affecting internal validity highlight the need for high-quality head-to-head comparative studies to draw more robust conclusions.
title: Potential of multimedia-supported informed consent in clinical practice: a systematic review

summary: To investigate the associations between paternal antidepressant use during spermatogenesis and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring. Nationwide population based cohort study. Danish national registers. 1 365 887 liveborn singleton infants in Denmark from 2000 to 2023, followed from birth until 31 December 2023, death, emigration, or first occurrence of outcome, whichever came first. Metabolic disorders in offspring, including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and overweight or obesity, were identified from hospital and prescription records. Offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during spermatogenesis (three months before pregnancy) were compared with those of fathers who did not take antidepressants during this period and fathers who used antidepressants only during pregnancy to further account for underlying paternal mental health conditions. Associations between paternal antidepressant use and metabolic disorders, collectively and individually, were estimated as propensity score weighted hazard ratios using Cox regression. 23 572 (1.7%) offspring were born to fathers who used antidepressants during spermatogenesis. During a mean follow-up of 12.1 years (standard deviation 7.0 years), 18 353 (1.3%) offspring were diagnosed with a metabolic disorder, including 364 whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis and 17 989 whose fathers did not use antidepressants during this period (1.39 v 1.11 events per 1000 person years, respectively). Offspring whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis had a slightly higher risk of developing metabolic disorders (weighted hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04 to 1.38) compared with offspring who were unexposed. The associations varied by specific metabolic outcomes, with weighted hazard ratios ranging from 0.81 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.47) for hypercholesterolaemia to 1.64 (95% CI 1.21 to 2.22) for hypertension. However, when compared with offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during the pregnancy period only, no increased risk was found of any metabolic disorders (0.75, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.98) or of specific metabolic disorders. The slightly increased risk of metabolic disorders in offspring of fathers using antidepressants during spermatogenesis was probably attributable to underlying paternal mental health disorders. These findings offer reassurance for men treated with antidepressants before pregnancy.
title: Preconception antidepressant use in fathers and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring: Danish population based cohort study.

summary: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares are common and unpredictable. Current monitoring relies on episodic clinical visits and laboratory testing, thereby limiting the ability to anticipate disease worsening. Wearable devices may support continuous remote monitoring, but models must account for missing real-world data, heterogeneous consumer devices, and the distinction between symptomatic disease activity and systemic inflammation. Objective: The study aimed to develop and evaluate deep learning (DL) time-series models using wearable-derived physiological data to predict symptomatic and inflammatory RA flares up to 28 days in advance. Methods: In a prospective cohort study, adults with RA used a smartwatch (Apple Watch; Apple Inc), a wearable fitness tracker (Fitbit; Google LLC), or a smart ring (Oura Ring; Oura Health Oy). Daily wearable-derived heart rate, heart rate variability, and step-count were harmonized across devices and linked with smartphone-based patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and available C-reactive protein results. Symptomatic flares were defined using longitudinal RAPID3 (Routine Assessment of Patient Index Data 3) scores, and inflammatory flares were defined using a prespecified C-reactive protein threshold. Classical machine learning and DL models were trained to predict daily flare vs remission status at 0-, 7-, 14-, 21-, and 28-day horizons. Model evaluation used a temporally ordered 70/30 within-participant train-test split. Performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROCAUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and participant-level sensitivity. This prediction-model analysis was not prospectively registered. Results: Forty-nine participants contributed 5624 days of overlapping wearable and clinical data. Participants used Apple Watch (n=31), Fitbit (n=15), or Oura Ring (n=3). DL models outperformed machine learning models using imputed wearable data, with average ROCAUC improvements of 5.3% for symptomatic flares and 18.4% for inflammatory flares, and AUPRC improvements of 9.3% and 44.1%, respectively. For 7-day-ahead prediction, transformer models incorporating wearable-derived physiology and demographic features achieved ROCAUCs of 0.95 for both symptomatic and inflammatory flares, with AUPRCs of 0.92 and 0.91, respectively. Adding daily PRO improved participant-level sensitivity for inflammatory flare prediction from 0.67 to 0.87. Performance remained stable across prediction horizons for up to 4 weeks. Conclusions: Wearable-derived physiological signals analyzed with DL may support personalized forecasting of symptomatic and inflammatory RA flare states weeks in advance. By integrating passive digital biomarkers with PROs, this approach offers a scalable framework for proactive RA monitoring that could help identify disease exacerbations earlier than episodic clinical assessment alone. Further validation in larger, more diverse cohorts and prospective studies is needed to determine whether wearable-guided forecasting improves clinical decision-making, timely intervention, and long-term outcomes.
title: Predicting Rheumatoid Arthritis Flares Using Wearable Device Data: Deep Learning Study

summary: To assess whether prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Population based cohort study. Nationwide register data on births, dispensed drugs, and specialist healthcare diagnoses from Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. 3 643 376 children born in 2000-21 followed up for a median 9 years after birth in Sweden and 10 years in Norway and Denmark. Prenatal exposure, defined as ≥1 filled prescription for ADHD drug treatment anytime during pregnancy or in the second/third trimester (≥98 days after the last menstrual period). Analyses were also done for monotherapy with methylphenidate, amphetamines, and atomoxetine. Unexposed pregnancies had no filled prescriptions for ADHD drugs during pregnancy. Neurodevelopmental disorders (any, subgroups, and individual disorders), identified on the basis of inpatient and outpatient diagnoses in specialist healthcare. Propensity score overlap weighted Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted (weighted) hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Data from Denmark were analysed separately, and results were pooled using random effects meta-analysis. 7595 (0.2%) children were prenatally exposed to any ADHD drug (5230 methylphenidate, 1510 amphetamines, 553 atomoxetine only). About one third (n=2389) were exposed in the second/third trimester. After control for confounders, neither any nor second/third trimester exposure to ADHD drugs overall or by drug type was associated with increased risk of any neurodevelopmental disorder (weighted hazard ratio 1.05, 95% confidence interval 0.98 to 1.12), behavioural and emotional disorders (1.04, 0.97 to 1.12), or disorders of psychological and intellectual development (1.06, 0.96 to 1.18). Some elevated hazard ratios for infrequent outcomes were observed but not consistently identified across analyses. This multinational cohort study found no increased risk of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders associated with prenatal exposure to ADHD drugs. These findings strengthen existing evidence and can assist pregnant people and clinicians in weighing the benefits and risks of such treatment during pregnancy.
title: Prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and risk of neurodevelopmental disorders: Scandinavian multinational cohort study.

summary: Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (mTLE) is a common drug-resistant epilepsy. Temporal lobe resection is the most effective treatment, but postoperative recurrence and antiseizure medication (ASM) withdrawal remain major clinical challenges. Existing prediction tools are limited by endpoint specificity, restricted external validation, and lack of integration into sequential postoperative management pathways. We developed a sequential modelling strategy in mTLE, spanning recurrence prediction to ASM withdrawal risk stratification. In phase 1, postoperative recurrence models were developed and validated using 52 preoperative multimodal features in 1278 patients across cohorts 1–4 (three retrospective, one prospective). Five top-ranked models achieved AUCs of 0.926–0.932 (internal) and 0.830–0.931 (three external sets), with a three-tier (low/intermediate/high) risk stratification. In phase 2, ASM withdrawal recurrence models were developed and validated in 679 seizure-free, phase 1 low/intermediate-risk patients eligible for withdrawal across cohorts 5–8 (three retrospective, one prospective). Five top-ranked models achieved AUCs of 0.897–0.902 (internal) and 0.789–0.933 (three external sets), with risk stratification for individualized withdrawal estimation. Models showed good calibration, net clinical benefit, and SHAP-based interpretability. A research-based risk-estimation web tool was developed to support potential clinical translation. This promising modelling strategy integrates population-level risk stratification with individualized prediction, providing preliminary postoperative guidance: high-recurrence-risk patients may not be ideal for early ASM withdrawal despite seizure freedom, while low-risk patients may be considered for earlier withdrawal evaluation. Given the primarily retrospective design and relatively small phase 2 prospective cohort, further prospective external validation and clinical-impact studies are required before routine implementation.
title: Sequential framework for predicting postoperative recurrence and antiseizure-medication withdrawal risk in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy

summary: Background: Medical vision-language models combine images and text to answer questions, generate reports, and support image interpretation. Task accuracy alone does not establish whether their outputs depend on relevant visual evidence or remain reliable under changes in the input. Objective: This study aimed to describe how trustworthiness is evaluated in medical vision-language models, identify gaps in evaluation and reporting, and develop a preliminary minimum evaluation checklist. Methods: We conducted a scoping review using the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews). We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and IEEE Xplore for English-language publications from January 1, 2022, to March 25, 2026. Eligible reports were peer-reviewed full papers that evaluated an image-and-language model in a medical imaging context and reported a measured result on at least 1 of 8 trustworthiness dimensions. One reviewer charted the studies, and a second verified the extraction. We summarized evaluation practices descriptively and applied the proposed 8-item MiTEC (Minimum Trustworthiness Evaluation Checklist) retrospectively. We did not perform a risk-of-bias appraisal. Results: We identified 516 records, screened 506 database records based on the title and abstract, and assessed 72 unique reports after merging duplicate full-text entries. The revised synthesis includes 29 studies: 11 journal articles and 18 conference papers. Robustness was evaluated in 37.9% (11/29), hallucination in 24.1% (7/29), distribution shift in 20.7% (6/29), and visual grounding in 17.2% (5/29). Interpretability and fairness were each evaluated in 13.8% (4/29), uncertainty or confidence reliability in 6.9% (2/29), and safety in 3.4% (1/29). Two studies used a text-only baseline, and 4 used at least 1 image-reliance control. No included study was confirmed to report a formal calibration metric or a selective-prediction curve. Retrospective MiTEC scoring identified 41 (17.7%) reported items among 232 study-item pairs. Conclusions: Evaluation practices varied across the included studies. Image-reliance controls, formal calibration measures, and subgroup analyses were uncommon. MiTEC is an author-proposed item set that requires independent testing and stakeholder consensus. The findings describe the included sample; incomplete linkage of preprints to published versions limits claims about the wider literature.
title: Trustworthiness Evaluation of Medical Vision-Language Models: Scoping Review and Proposed Minimum Evaluation Checklist
